results.summary:
ADR-004's rename list is landed in one docs/strings PR (#69, draft, branch worktree-kb-66-1). No behaviour change: no code path, label, or attempt-history value was touched, and the test suite is untouched (427 pass — two of those arrived with #68, which landed under me mid-task).

All 7 items done:
1. Exit code 4 added to both exit-code lists — protocol.md's "Exit codes" section and the cli.js global help (which now spans three lines; the help text renders aligned). Wording: the dispatcher loop gave itself up, only `hkb dispatch --loop` ever exits 4, and a supervisor (cron/systemd/Actions) or the operator starts a fresh one.
2. `--reviewer <profile>` -> `--reviewer <github-user>`, matching lifecycle.js:226-237 (isGithubUser + requested_reviewers). Fixed at 4 sites, not the 2 the card listed: SKILL.md:63, cli.js help, plus protocol.md:212 and cli.js's request-review usage-error string — leaving `<profile>` in the same file that now says "always a GitHub user" would have contradicted the new glossary.
3. "fake-gh harness" -> "fake-gh test double" at all 4 sites: cli.js:429, model.js:434 (worker-facing deny message), SKILL.md:66, CLAUDE.md:26. Verified nothing stale in templates/, .agents/, web/, hooks/.
4. context.js:10 now says "the operator", killing the contradiction with context.js:107. The function name `isHumanComment` is deliberately unchanged (code untouched).
5. SKILL.md:12 subtitle is now "the board protocol".
6. Bare "runner" qualified: README ×7 (track runner in the claude-track paragraph, Actions runner in the Actions section), docs/harnesses.md ×3, and one cli.js comment. Bare "runner" inside protocol.md's *Tracks* section and SKILL.md's *When you run a track* is left as-is — the section establishes the sense, and the new glossary now draws the track-runner/Actions-runner line explicitly.
7. protocol.md gains a "## Glossary" table at the top: three seats (operator/dispatcher/worker) in bold, vocabulary (reviewer/track runner/profile/host/supervisor) in italic, each with an "Is"/"Is not" column. The attempts-schema row now documents the reserved synthetic `profile` values — `dispatcher` (tick wrote the row, out of retries), `reviewer` (`hkb request-changes`), `human` (operator by hand, verified against lifecycle.js:60 — it is `task.agent || 'human'`, so only on a task with no `kb:agent:*` label) — plus "do not name a board profile after one of them".

Nothing on the "deliberately unchanged" list was touched.

WIKI, for the next worker: docs/wiki/decisions/adr-004-roles-and-adoption.md reports STALE and I left it that way on purpose. It covers context.js, cli.js, SKILL.md, protocol.md (all mine) and dispatch.js (already moved by #68 before I rebased). Its Context section anchors every file:line claim to commit 6c0e81f, so re-stamping would rewrite generated_at_commit and bless prose against code it was never written against — and docs/wiki/AGENTS.md says a stale decision record is a prompt to consider a superseding record, not to edit or re-stamp it. ADR-004 still has consequences outstanding (the "Who runs a board: the seats" docs section), so whoever closes those out should decide the ADR's fate. By contrast architecture/overview WAS re-stamped and is fresh: the churn under it is comments and help strings only, and no claim on the page changed; a log.md line records that.

REBASE NOTE: #68 (manual-attempt reclaim) landed on main mid-task and conflicted in protocol.md's attempts row and docs/wiki/log.md. Both resolved by keeping both sides. While merging I also applied item 4's rename to #68's new sentence: "a human claimed it" -> "the operator claimed it".
